topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer treatments and their mechanisms of action.

topics.label: Surgical and radiation therapies in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines localized treatment approaches, emphasizing the role of surgical resection, radiotherapy, and early detection in tumor removal.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy and drug resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the mechanisms of action, systemic toxicities, and efflux-mediated drug resistance associated with conventional cytotoxic chemotherapy.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies designed to exploit intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities, including hormone dependencies, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction and small-molecule kinase inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the rationale of oncogene addiction alongside the therapeutic mechanisms, structural targeting, and resistance pathways of small-molecule kinase inhibitors.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the design and therapeutic actions of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates directed against tumor cell-surface markers.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell-based treatments
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine tumor immune surveillance and methods to harness or engineer T cells to destroy cancer cells using checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific engagers, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Challenges, historical progress, and future perspectives in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate broad clinical challenges, historical improvements in patient survival, and emerging future strategies in cancer management.
